學校簡介 
IDRAC Business School is signatory to the ERASMUS Charter and offers Study Abroad programs to all his 
partners with 2 programs fully taught in English and 1 in French. 
All of them are course packages: students can get up to 30 ECTS in each program. Each student can 
choose the program that best fits his needs but cannot mix courses from different programs in order to avoid 
schedule clashes. 
The IDRAC Business School BBA program in English is opened in Lyon and Paris for fall and spring 
semesters. Bordeaux, Montpellier and Nantes campuses open for spring semester. The program in French 
is available on 9 different campuses. 
The PGE in English is opened in Lyon both during fall and spring semesters and allows to be mixed up with 
French students. This program received the Grade de Master (one of the highest recognition given by the 
Ministry of education to a program in France). 
All our programs offer the possibility to learn French as a foreign language. Students can enroll in the French 
seminar at the start of the semester, intensive seminar in French. And classes are programmed regularly 
during the semester.

基百科） 
國立土魯斯應用科學學院是一所位於法國西南城市土魯斯的工程師類大學，屬於法國國
立應用科學學院（INSA）集團五所學校的一所。學校創立於 1963 年，屬土魯斯大學
（Université de Toulouse）聯盟學校之一。是一所工程師教育及科學研究為一體的大學。
該校由法國高等教育部以及負責頒發工程師文憑的法國工程師教育協會授權，負責工程
師培養和科學研究工作。 INSA 土魯斯的工程師學位課程學制為學+碩共五年。

original_evidence.text:
Housing in Munich unfortunately is a major issue. We are only able to house 
about 50% to 60% of our incoming students in student residence halls (they 
are subsidized by the state and therefore only cost around 280 to 360 Euro). 
Since there is no fair way to distribute the rooms, we use a lottery system in 
order to assign them. Those who are not lucky need to find a room on the 
private market. Although we do assist students by handing out information 
on how to find affordable housing, it is up to the student to find 
accommodation. Private rooms are much more expensive (starting at around 
500 Euro in shared apartments) and students should also consider living in 
the suburbs or towns along the regional train lines.

All students are responsible for their own insurance arrangements and we strong recommend t hat you take 
a comprehensive insurance for your stay in Finland. Before leaving your home country, please check your 
travel and health insurance. 
Students from outside the EU / EEA must have private insurance to cover the duration of the visa / 
residence permit and the Schengen area before they enter Finland. The insurance must cover the treatment 
and health care provided by municipal health care services, cases of illness or accident, and include travel 
costs to home country as well as liability insurance. The health insurance must cover the costs of medical 
care up to 100,000 Euros.

Students coming from EU countries do not need visa. Other international students 
can get information about visa application procedure at the Czech embassies or 
consulates in their home countries or they can consult the website of the Ministry of 
Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic. To be able to get the visa confirmed after your 
arrival at Immigration department, you must be insured for the whole period of your 
stay. We recommend you to administrate the health insurance in your country before 
departure. If you need VISA, ask at the Czech Embassy/Consulate in your home 
country about procedure; remember than you need the forms from us and Visa 
applications should be submitted to the Embassy at least 60 days before the planned 
date of departure. It is not possible to apply for the visa in the Czech Republic.

Students coming from EU countries do not need visa. Other international students 
can get information about visa application procedure at the Czech embassies or 
consulates in their home countries or they can consult the website of the Ministry of 
Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic. To be able to get the visa confirmed after your 
arrival at Immigration department, you must be insured for the whole period of your 
stay. We recommend you to administrate the health insurance in your country before 
departure. If you need VISA, ask at the Czech Embassy/Consulate in your home 
country about procedure; remember than you need the forms from us and Visa 
applications should be submitted to the Embassy at least 60 days before the planned 
date of departure. It is not possible to apply for the visa in the Czech Republic.

阿爾滕巴斯大學是土耳其伊斯坦堡的基礎大學。該大學成立於 2008 年，原名為伊斯坦
堡凱梅爾布爾加茲大學，並於 2017 年更名為現名。阿爾滕巴斯大學擁有來自 89 個國
家的 5,000 多名國際學生，其中約 40% 的學生是國際學生。

Access to our online application portal including the application guide will be provided

Course information  View UM Courses 
 
 Level of studies and 
admission criteria  
Undergraduate admission is not competitive in most study areas if students are 
in good academic standing defined by their home institution and meet the 
language proficiency requirements. The selection of the inbound applicants is 
at the discretion of relevant Faculty/office at the University of Manitoba.  
 
Graduate-level admission (Master and Ph. D) is competitive. Students may need to 
meet additional criteria. Completion of a four-year undergraduate program* is 
required for graduate admission. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (B or equivalent) in the 
last two full years of study is also required.   
*Students who completed a three-year undergraduate program are not eligible for 
our Graduate-level admission. They are eligible to apply for our undergraduate 
program to take courses at 1000 to 4000 level (highest).   
Official transcripts of courses 
and grades/results 
This document must be in English or an official translated copy. Upload this document 
as a .pdf file. Description of grading (grading scale) on your university letterhead 
must also be included.   
Study plan A detailed study plan is submitted within the online portal.  
 Personal statement One- to two-page personal statement of intent, uploaded as a .doc - include the 
following: 
• Why do you want to come to the University of Manitoba on exchange? 
• What personal, academic, and professional goals do you hope to achieve on 
exchange at the University of Manitoba?

Within the online application portal 
 
Application for exchange 
student admission 
Access to our online application portal including the application guide will be provided 
to the student and the exchange coordinator by email after receiving nomination from 
the partner university’s exchange coordinator. 
Course information  View UM Courses 
 
 Level of studies and 
admission criteria  
Undergraduate admission is not competitive in most study areas if students are 
in good academic standing defined by their home institution and meet the 
language proficiency requirements. The selection of the inbound applicants is 
at the discretion of relevant Faculty/office at the University of Manitoba.  
 
Graduate-level admission (Master and Ph. D) is competitive. Students may need to 
meet additional criteria. Completion of a four-year undergraduate program* is 
required for graduate admission. A minimum GPA of 3.0 (B or equivalent) in the 
last two full years of study is also required.   
*Students who completed a three-year undergraduate program are not eligible for 
our Graduate-level admission. They are eligible to apply for our undergraduate 
program to take courses at 1000 to 4000 level (highest).   
Official transcripts of courses 
and grades/results 
This document must be in English or an official translated copy. Upload this document 
as a .pdf file. Description of grading (grading scale) on your university letterhead 
must also be included.   
Study plan A detailed study plan is submitted within the online portal.  
 Personal statement One- to two-page personal statement of intent, uploaded as a .doc - include the 
following: 
• Why do you want to come to the University of Manitoba on exchange? 
• What personal, academic, and professional goals do you hope to achieve on 
exchange at the University of Manitoba?

2027/28 UNIVERSITY OF MANITOBA EXCHANGE INFORMATION SHEET 
 
Other important information   
Other fees While tuition fees are waived, students will be required to pay student organization fees 
(approximately $150 per term) and potentially field trip and lab fees, if applicable. Students 
can expect to pay $100-200 per course for books and can sell them back at the end of each 
term to get a portion of the money back. 
Housing On-Campus Student Residences are strongly recommended. There are several options for 
residence, from private rooms with meal plans to a shared suite with private rooms 
without meal plans. 
Study permit, 
visa, E-Travel Authorization 
Learn about which immigration document you will need on the Immigration 
Information for Inbound Exchange Students webpage.  Admitted exchange students 
with questions about their applications will be able to contact UM’s International 
Student Advisors for assistance. 
Health insurance Exchange students are required to purchase travel health insurance from their home 
country. Choice of insurance is at the discretion of students.  
 Health and Wellness Student’s health and mental well-being are very important. Visit our Health and 
Wellness page for all resources and supports available for all students including 
exchange students.  
Cannabis legislation Cannabis is now legal in Canada for individuals 19 years of age or older. Visit the Health 
and Wellness page for information on the University of Manitoba policy.  
Accessibility Services UM’s Student Accessibility Services (SAS) provides support for students with disabilities. 
Please visit the SAS website for information on registering for their services. 
Information about Winnipeg 
and Manitoba 
www.tourismwinnipeg.com 
www.winnipeg.ca  
www.travelmanitoba.com  
 
International student program information 
 
International exchange 
student orientation 
Students will learn about the University of Manitoba and Winnipeg from staff and a 
panel of local students. They will also enjoy a meal a n d   make new friends from all over 
the world!  
 
Excursions and special events IC Exchange Program invites all students to join excursions & social events through 
their exchange.  Previous years’ activities include: hockey games, Hallowe’en 
party, visit to the Canadian Museum for Human Rights, football games, ice skating, 
board game café, tours and more.  
IC Exchange Buddy Program 
 
We connect inbound exchange students with a buddy, a UM student who has 
returned from their exchange abroad. Students will have the opportunity to 
connect with their buddy virtually before arrival and meet in-person after arrival 
to support inbound exchange student adjustment to UM and Winnipeg.

2027/28 UNIVERSITY OF MANITOBA EXCHANGE INFORMATION SHEET 
 
Other important information   
Other fees While tuition fees are waived, students will be required to pay student organization fees 
(approximately $150 per term) and potentially field trip and lab fees, if applicable. Students 
can expect to pay $100-200 per course for books and can sell them back at the end of each 
term to get a portion of the money back. 
Housing On-Campus Student Residences are strongly recommended. There are several options for 
residence, from private rooms with meal plans to a shared suite with private rooms 
without meal plans. 
Study permit, 
visa, E-Travel Authorization 
Learn about which immigration document you will need on the Immigration 
Information for Inbound Exchange Students webpage.  Admitted exchange students 
with questions about their applications will be able to contact UM’s International 
Student Advisors for assistance. 
Health insurance Exchange students are required to purchase travel health insurance from their home 
country. Choice of insurance is at the discretion of students.  
 Health and Wellness Student’s health and mental well-being are very important. Visit our Health and 
Wellness page for all resources and supports available for all students including 
exchange students.  
Cannabis legislation Cannabis is now legal in Canada for individuals 19 years of age or older. Visit the Health 
and Wellness page for information on the University of Manitoba policy.  
Accessibility Services UM’s Student Accessibility Services (SAS) provides support for students with disabilities. 
Please visit the SAS website for information on registering for their services. 
Information about Winnipeg 
and Manitoba 
www.tourismwinnipeg.com 
www.winnipeg.ca  
www.travelmanitoba.com  
 
International student program information 
 
International exchange 
student orientation 
Students will learn about the University of Manitoba and Winnipeg from staff and a 
panel of local students. They will also enjoy a meal a n d   make new friends from all over 
the world!  
 
Excursions and special events IC Exchange Program invites all students to join excursions & social events through 
their exchange.  Previous years’ activities include: hockey games, Hallowe’en 
party, visit to the Canadian Museum for Human Rights, football games, ice skating, 
board game café, tours and more.  
IC Exchange Buddy Program 
 
We connect inbound exchange students with a buddy, a UM student who has 
returned from their exchange abroad. Students will have the opportunity to 
connect with their buddy virtually before arrival and meet in-person after arrival 
to support inbound exchange student adjustment to UM and Winnipeg.

2027/28 UNIVERSITY OF MANITOBA EXCHANGE INFORMATION SHEET 
 
Intercultural Leaders Program Open to all students, this dynamic and interactive program runs for eight 
sessions each fall and winter term. Through a variety of group sessions and 
workshops, students will enhance cultural awareness and develop intercultural 
skills. Students will also strengthen leadership, public speaking, conflict 
resolution, and communication and facilitation skills. Participants will build a 
stronger sense of self-confidence they can take beyond the classroom to their 
personal and professional lives. 
Language Exchange 
Program 
This program matches volunteers with complementary interests in language and culture. 
Students meet with their conversation partners every week to practice each other’s 
languages and learn about each other’s cultures. The sessions are friendly and informal. 
 
Other opportunities for students 
 
Sports and recreation Our new Active Living Centre is a world-class facility, offering students many options 
including: recreational sports leagues, climbing wall, swimming pool, hockey, tennis, 
soccer, rugby, badminton, ultimate frisbee, volleyball, fitness classes, yoga and much 
more! 
Student communities & 
groups 
Connect with UM student communities and over 200 student groups representing a 
diverse range of interests. Popular groups include: Photography, Anime, Amnesty 
International, Choir, Robotics, cultural groups, Swing Dance, Gaming, Parks Canada 
Campus, UM Snow (snowboarding), Rainbow Pride Mosaic, Indigenous Students’ 
Association and the Womyn’s Centre. 
Academic support Academic Learning Centre 
Student Accessibility Services 
Academic Integrity 
Travel Many students take advantage of Winnipeg’s central location to travel north to 
Churchill to see the famous polar bears, west to the Rocky Mountains, east to Toronto 
or Montreal or even south to the United States. Near and within Winnipeg, students can 
explore abundant nature, forests, lakes, beaches, rivers and parks.

original_evidence.text:
Important Changes and Notes Regarding the SDW : Sandwich 
Program (Coursework-Based Exchange) 
     NEW / Important Changes 
1. Graduate-Level Course Enrollment Restriction (Effective Spring 2027)   
 From Spring Semester 2027, undergraduate students participating in the SDW Program will 
no longer be allowed to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Students should consider this change when preparing study plans and discussing credit 
transfer arrangements with their home institution.  
 Until the Spring 2027 course list is published, students should refer to the current 
timetable for reference. 
 
2026 Grade 1 Exchange Program Exchange Program Student (Undergraduate) | Shibaura 
Institute of Technology Timetable Search 
 
 
2. Special Provision for Students from Five-Year Integrated Degree Programs 
 Students enrolled in integrated five-year degree programs may be considered academically 
equivalent to master's students during their senior years.  
 Eligible students may continue to enroll in graduate-level courses.  
 Partner institutions must explain which year(s) of their program are considered master's-
level equivalent.  
 Supporting documentation must be submitted through the TAO application system by the 
nominator. 
 
3. Mandatory Submission of Financial Support Documentation  
 Due to stricter immigration screening procedures, all student visa applicants must provide 
proof of financial capability.  
 Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be provided in 
the application system.  
 Supporting documents must be uploaded through the TAO application system.
original_evidence.applicability: 芝浦2027年變更說明；SDW與REP分別適用，非完整年度申請包。

original_evidence.text:
4. Research Activities for SDW Participants 
Eligibility 
 Only students enrolled in the SDW Program for two semesters (one academic year) are 
eligible. 
 
Requirements 
Students wishing to conduct research activities must: 
 Apply during the same application period as the REP (Research Exchange Program). 
 Obtain prior approval from the prospective academic supervisor (laboratory faculty 
member). 
 Submit the same application documents required for the REP Program, including:  
o Curriculum Vitae (CV) 
o Research Proposal 
o Any other required supporting documents 
 Pay the facility usage fee specified in the REP Program application guidelines. 
 
Important Notes 
 Research activities will only be permitted after all required application procedures have 
been completed and approved. 
 Final approval is subject to review by both the University and the prospective academic 
supervisor. 
 
 
5. No Extension of the SDW Program During Enrollment  
 
 Effective from Fall 2026, students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to extend 
their participation in the Sandwich Program during their period of enrollment. Applicants 
must carefully decide at the time of application whether to register for one semester or 
two semesters. 
 Please note that students who enroll for one semester are not permitted to switch from the 
Sandwich Program to the REP Program, as stated in Item 4 above.

screening procedures for student visa applications. As a result, all students applying for a 
student visa will be required to provide documentation demonstrating sufficient financial 
resources to support themselves during their stay in Japan.

• All student visa applicants must submit financial support documentation. 
• Applicants must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to cover their living expenses 
during their stay. Details regarding the estimated monthly living expenses will be 
provided in the application system.

Online Application System. Applicants will be required to upload the designated 
supporting documents through TAO.

original_evidence.text:
3. Extension of the Study Period 
Students Entering Japan with a Short-Term Visa 
 Students who participate in the program under a short-term visa are not eligible to extend 
their study period under any circumstances.  
 Students should carefully determine their intended period of study before submitting their 
application. 
 
Students Holding a Student Visa 
 Students who wish to extend their study period while holding a student visa must notify the 
International Office at least two months prior to their scheduled completion date.  
 Applicants seeking an extension are required to submit the prescribed application documents.  
 If the extension results in a total study period of 182 days or longer, an additional facility 
usage fee of JPY 47,000 will be charged.  
 Approval of an extension is subject to the University's review and procedures. 
 
 
！Important Information 
4. Selection of a Prospective Academic Supervisor  
SIT does not publish a directory of faculty contact information. In addition, the application 
process differs depending on the applicant's circumstances. Applicants should apply according 
to one of the following categories. 
■ Case 1: Applicants Who Have Obtained Prior Consent from a Faculty Member  
• This category applies to students who already have an academic connection with an SIT 
faculty member and have discussed the possibility of supervision in advance. 
• Applicants may designate that faculty member as their Prospective Academic Supervisor 
in their application. 
■ Case 2: Applicants Without a Prospective Academic Supervisor  
• This category applies to students who do not have an existing connection with an SIT 
faculty member. 
• Applicants may refer to the faculty list for applicants without a designated supervisor, 
which is available on the SIT website. 
• Applicants may indicate up to three preferred faculty members in order of preference in 
their application. 
• Based on the applicant's preferences and academic background, SIT will conduct the 
supervisor matching process.

original_evidence.text:
Pukyong National University
Fact Sheet for Exchange Programs
 EXCHANGE PROGRAM INFORMATION
Courses Most of courses are taught in Korean, but a variety of courses 
are offered in English. The list of courses taught in English will 
be available one or two months prior to each semester. The list 
will be sent to all accepted exchange students by Email with 
instructions on course registration. Exchange students can take 
up to 18 academic credits per semester. If students would like 
to learn Korean Language, they could participate in the Korean 
Language Program during the semester with 30% discounted 
price.
All courses at PKNU are credit-bearing and are recognized by 
most universities and institutions.
Credit Transfer
Grading Scale
     Housing
However, it is better that students consult academic officials 
at their home universities about credit transfer prior to the 
program begins. It is students’ responsibility to consult 
properly, and it is their home university’s authority to decide 
on the credit transfer.
*3 Credit Hours: 45 contact hours
*2 Credit Hours: 30 contact hours

All exchange students are automatically assigned to a room 
(shared) at on-campus dormitories. The dormitory fee for one 
semester is around KRW 2,000,000 which includes three meals 
per day at the cafeteria. Students can find an accommodation 
outside the campus if they want.
National Health Insurance              All exchange students are required to enroll Korean National
Health Insurance. They will be automatically enrolled on the 
same day of alien registration after they arrive in Korea. They 
have to pay about KRW 100,000 per month. More detailed 
information will be provided to the accepted exchange 
students. Students staying in Korea for less than six months are 
not covered by Korean National Health Insurance. Therefore, 
they must obtain either international student or traveler 
insurance before departing for Korea to cover their entire stay. 
The university will not be responsible for any issues arising 
from insurance claims if students fail to secure proper 
coverage.
PKNU Student Buddy Program  PKNU student buddy will help exchange students adjust to a
new life at PKNU. The Buddy program application will be 
accepted at an exchange student orientation a few days before 
the start of the semester, after the students arrive in Korea.
